name: Why the canal works stood idle
subject: history
question: cause
brief: The old log book in the school library records that the works site beside the canal stopped work for two monsoons in the 1990s, and does not say why. You are the group's researcher: gather what the library, the council papers and the photographs offer, and the group will explain the cause. Nobody else in the group is willing to argue the other side, so every limit you name you will have to think of yourself.

claims.name: Repeated floods put the pump house out of use
The council stopped paying for the pump contract
A workers' strike halted the site
A fire at the depot destroyed the pumps

evidence.name: The canal gauge in the log shows water over the pump-house sill on fourteen days
A dated photograph shows water at the pump-house doorstep
The tender register shows the pump contract unpaid for eleven months
Council minutes record two requests for more money turned down
The attendance rolls show full gangs on every dry day of both years
An inspector's note records the pumps intact and no fire damage
The log notes the Durga Puja holidays in October

limitations.name: The log was kept by someone watching the canal, not by the council
Three months of the tender register are missing
Floods and an unpaid contract could have worked together; the sources cannot separate them
The log was recopied in 2003, so copying errors are possible

note: The canal-side works site is from INDIA_WORLD_BIBLE.md (loc_canal_works). The archive, the log and the dates are invented. Two causes are defensible and may both be true; the limitation says so.
